title: Global finite-order families and residual tests
reviewed_arguments: H0 states uniform complete order-m estimates and uniform rapid tails outside a fixed compact normalized cone; each member being separately residual is explicitly weaker.
L0 constructs one collar interval only on the relevant compact boundary neighborhood, retaining all cross-chart/component corner terms and the original flat-input Banach bound.
L1 uses J*J=theta^2, not identity, and proves BDJ=r from the exact complete input support. No division by a vanishing cutoff or bounded inverse diagonal is asserted.
L2 reuses the full positive square-root series without injectivity, proves compact support, and uses a second larger frame to reconstruct the smooth joint kernel through the cutoff transition.
L3 proves the partial isometry on the orthogonal complement of the kernel and extends it by zero; its contraction suffices for the full density-correct normal factor.
A0 constructs an actual full positive scalar Q=sum B_i*B_i, with prescribed compact microsupport and nonnegative elliptic principal symbol on the common compact cone.
A1 and A2 retain the complete global parametrix, order-zero factors, proper/low-frequency/cross-chart residuals and every negative-order uniform remainder estimate.

T0 proves exactly two scalar test norms plus the original Banach remainder on the arbitrary manifold. G0 extends only the actual smooth graph and retains the single-scalar gluing and full observation-graph obligations.
Three solutions check noninjective compact frames, the exact failure of a squared residual norm to dominate its factor, and a uniformly order-zero but not uniformly residual high-frequency family.
